relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with clinically suspected but genetically unconfirmed ATS: 'Suspecting arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS), attendants were counseled for further genetic evaluation, but unfortunately, they have been lost to follow-up.'
method_note: Hand extraction from a short case report (no tables). The patient has a clinical/imaging suspicion of arterial tortuosity syndrome only; no SLC2A10 testing was done ('we were unable to confirm it through genetic testing'), so the variants table is empty. He was included as in scope on the basis of the authors' working diagnosis of ATS; downstream users may prefer to exclude him because the diagnosis is unconfirmed. n_patients_reported left null: the authors state no patient with an SLC2A10 variant. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (no statement). Country recorded as 'resident of Iraq' (residence, not stated ancestry). Normal findings recorded per D-27: 'developmentally normal' -> developmental delay excluded; 'Anthropometry was normal' recorded as 'abnormal anthropometry' excluded (a whole-examination statement, nothing more specific excluded); 'normal biventricular function' -> ventricular dysfunction excluded; 'trileaflet aortic valve' -> bicuspid aortic valve excluded; 'normal right brachiocephalic, common carotid and subclavian arteries' recorded as written. 'No hernia ... was noted' (examination) used to exclude the checklist item inguinal hernia but not diaphragmatic/hiatal hernia (an internal hernia an external examination does not address). 'No ... skin laxity' recorded as a phenotypic_features exclusion, but the composite checklist item 'hyperextensible or lax skin (cutis laxa)' left not reported because hyperextensibility was not addressed. Dilated aortic root/annulus (Z score + 4.52) mapped to checklist 'aortic root aneurysm' as observed. Echocardiography and CT give slightly different measurements (annulus 16 mm vs 17 mm; Aao 56 mm vs 55 x 57 mm); both quoted, not a contradiction of presence. Discussion statements about ATS in general were not applied to the patient. No contradictions found.
